architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 °C melt residence, indicating unresolved thermal-hold instability.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal hold showed SI_15_60 = 0.5154, corresponding to a 51.54% viscosity increase from 15 to 60 min at 120 °C, and SI_15_90 = 0.9308, corresponding to a 93.08% increase from 15 to 90 min. By contrast, E1 increased by 9.51% and 16.85% over the same respective windows, establishing large formulation-dependent hold drift.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have local 120 °C hold trajectories, each represented by one four-point run over 15–90 min. No hold data are available for E2 or any candidate on the independent acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes. In contrast, temperature response is measured at six temperatures from 80 to 130 °C across multiple formulations and runs, and realized viscosity-level uncertainty is directly exposed by three E2 runs with CV values of 0.46–0.58 and max/min ratios of 2.80–3.57.
measurement_requirements: Measure the candidate under the matched-window M-HOLD-120 protocol at 120 °C, recording viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min.
Use at least two independent preparations and report each trajectory and SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 rather than only an averaged endpoint.
Compute the H-CORE prediction prospectively as E1 SI_15_60 multiplied by the candidate reactive mass fraction phi_r, using the exact audited candidate composition.

Compare the measured drift with both the linear-dilution prediction and the H-RESIN criterion of less than half that prediction, while applying the declared 2 percentage-point matched-window discrimination threshold.
Record preparation and thermal history so that a change in realized material state is not misattributed to modifier chemistry.

Include a matched realized-viscosity anchor, preferably at 110 °C with direct 120 and 130 °C verification, to distinguish viscosity-level relocation from alteration of the isothermal drift coordinate.

If the role of the minor tackifier axis is to be tested, use compositionally matched acrylic-only and acrylic-plus-tackifier experiments under the same hold protocol; a single dual-modifier formulation cannot establish tackifier necessity.
planner.scientific_question: At a resin-modified composition based on the E2 reactive core, is the repeated 15–60 min viscosity drift at 120 °C consistent with reactive-core linear dilution, or is it substantially below the dilution prediction, as required by the resin-modification/superlinear-suppression hypothesis?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-CORE vs H-DUAL: both predict approximately linear-dilution drift for an acrylic-only composition unless unexpectedly low drift falsifies H-DUAL; positive establishment of tackifier necessity requires a matched non-zero-tackifier arm

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: For phi_r = 0.80, H-CORE predicts 9.51% x 0.80 = 7.61% drift. If repeated SI_15_60 is below 3.80%, less than half that prediction, the result supports H-RESIN superlinear suppression, falsifies H-CORE, and—because the formulation contains no minor tackifier—falsifies H-DUAL's claim that tackifier is required to reach the low-drift regime.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If repeated SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified. Agreement with 7.61% within the declared 2 percentage-point resolution supports H-CORE. Such an acrylic-only result is consistent with H-DUAL but cannot establish tackifier necessity without a matched tackifier-containing experiment.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result from 3.80% to below 5.61% would be substantially below linear dilution beyond measurement resolution, falsifying H-CORE, but would not meet H-RESIN's registered half-linear acceptance threshold. A result from 5.61% to below 7.61% would remain resolution-compatible with H-CORE while not supporting H-RESIN. Repeat disagreement would indicate unresolved process-state variability rather than clean mechanistic discrimination.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, from at least two independent 120 C hold trajectories

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: The 20% acrylic plus 5% tackifier composition lies inside both supported intervention regions and directly tests H-CORE versus H-RESIN, but a single dual-axis result cannot test whether tackifier is necessary and therefore cannot falsify H-DUAL through an acrylic-only low-drift outcome.

The 15% acrylic-only hold offers similar hypothesis structure with a smaller modifier burden, but the 15% literature level has an unresolved fraction denominator and is only directional evidence, whereas 20% is repeatedly documented on a commensurate total-formulation basis.

The 25% acrylic-only level has direct analogue and comparative stability support, but it is a larger perturbation than the conservative 15-20% initial test band and therefore carries greater chemistry-transfer risk.
The anchor measurement addresses realized viscosity level through a shared-shape model rather than directly observing thermal-hold drift, so it does not adjudicate the registered drift hypotheses.

proposer.reasoning: S1C49 uses 20% acrylic-like modifier and no tackifier while preserving the E2 reactive-core proportions. The acrylic loading is inside the conservative externally supported 15-20% band and is repeatedly anchored near 20% by commensurate analogue formulations. M-HOLD-120 directly measures the least-resolved and decision-relevant isothermal drift coordinate without regression or extrapolation. Its predicted 7.61% linear drift and 3.80% superlinear-suppression threshold differ by more than the declared 2 percentage-point resolution. The zero-tackifier design also provides the only single-card route among the leading choices to falsify H-DUAL if acrylic alone reaches the registered low-drift regime, although it cannot positively prove tackifier necessity.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace the first run of S1C49::M-HOLD-120 with an E2 reactive-core-only matched-window hold, represented by S1C01::M-HOLD-120. Use its measured drift to define the E2-specific dilution reference before testing S1C49. The inventory contains several apparently indistinguishable reactive-core-only candidate IDs; S1C01 is selected as the first listed representative because no supplied fields distinguish them.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: The deterministic VOI score, tied top experiment set, and ranking were withheld, so membership of S1C49::M-HOLD-120 in that set cannot be established. This false value denotes unavailable top-set verification, not a demonstrated scored departure. Independently of the unavailable ranking, scientific evidence favors first measuring the E2 reactive-core baseline because the proposed 7.61% reference is transferred from compositionally and stoichiometrically different E1.
residual_decision_risk: The deterministic top set and all decision-stability quantities are withheld, so neither top-set membership nor sensitivity to weight perturbations can be verified.
S1C01 through S1C09 appear identical in the supplied inventory; unreported distinctions could affect which reactive-core control is appropriate.
Large E2 between-preparation viscosity-scale variation may also accompany variable hold behavior, requiring controlled histories, at least three preparations, and a prespecified aggregation rule.
An E2 baseline alone does not test H-RESIN or H-DUAL; S1C49 must subsequently be compared under matched conditions.
Without a verified non-reactive diluent arm, ordinary dilution remains entangled with acrylic-specific effects.
Acrylic OH or other NCO-reactive functionality has not been audited, so true reactive mass fraction and stoichiometry may differ from the nominal values.
H-DUAL has no registered numerical low-drift boundary, so an acrylic-only result cannot cleanly falsify it using H-RESIN's 3.80% threshold.
A matched acrylic-plus-tackifier arm remains necessary to test tackifier necessity, and a viscosity-level anchor remains necessary to distinguish drift suppression from viscosity-level relocation.
The E1 reference itself comes from a single hold run, so it remains a limited cross-formulation reference even after an E2 baseline is added.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection undermines the reference needed to interpret S1C49 rather than its directly measured SI_15_60 observable. S1C49 preserves the E2 reactive core, while the proposed H-CORE prediction uses the single E1 hold result despite differences in NCO:OH and MDI fraction. Running an E2 core-only M-HOLD-120 experiment first supplies the missing core-specific drift baseline and makes a later modified-arm comparison substantially more interpretable. It should use controlled preparation histories, preferably at least three independent preparations, and a prespecified repeat-combination rule. This baseline does not itself adjudicate acrylic suppression, but it removes the strongest obstacle before exposing the modified arm.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No weight-sensitivity assessment is possible from the supplied payload. top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, recommendation_flip_boundary, VOI weights, and the tied top set are all withheld. Therefore no specific perturbation can be identified as changing the decision, and the scientific defensibility of any such re-weighting cannot be evaluated.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: M-HOLD-120 directly measures values that can be at or above the stated 7.61% H-RESIN falsification boundary, so the criterion is attainable in principle. Its practical adjudication is incomplete because the proposal does not define how the minimum two repeats are combined, and the validity of 7.61% as the E2-based null prediction is not established.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result below 5.61% could falsify the registered numerical E1-scaled rule, but it would not establish that the E2 core exhibits superlinear resin suppression rather than a different undiluted baseline drift.
objections.objection: The claimed H-CORE versus H-RESIN separation uses 7.61% = 9.51% E1 drift x 0.80, but S1C49 preserves the E2 reactive core, not E1. E1 has NCO:OH = 1.70 and MDI fraction 0.19287, whereas E2 has NCO:OH = 1.80 and MDI fraction 0.20191. Because no E2 M-HOLD-120 baseline exists, the experiment cannot determine whether departure from 7.61% is caused by acrylic modification or by using the wrong core-specific reference coefficient. The numerical gap between 7.61% and 3.80% does exceed the declared 2 percentage-point resolution, but the uncertainty in the reference prediction is not included in that resolution.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The statement that an acrylic-only result below 3.80% falsifies H-DUAL would depend on an unregistered cross-hypothesis definition of 'low drift.'
objections.objection: The proposal treats SI_15_60 below 3.80% as entry into H-DUAL's 'low-drift regime,' although H-DUAL registers no numerical boundary for that regime. The 3.80% threshold belongs to H-RESIN's half-linear criterion and is imported into the H-DUAL adjudication without being defined there. The proposal correctly admits that a non-low acrylic-only result cannot establish tackifier necessity, but its claimed one-card falsification of H-DUAL lacks a registered quantitative threshold.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Observed suppression cannot uniquely be attributed to the H-RESIN account of reduced effective concentration and encounter frequency; it could instead arise from ordinary dilution relative to an unknown E2 baseline, altered NCO:OH stoichiometry, modifier reactivity, or realization-state changes.
objections.objection: S1C49 changes acrylic identity and reactive mass fraction simultaneously: it introduces 20% acrylic-like material while reducing the E2-derived reactive fraction to phi_r = 0.80. There is no matched 20% inert-diluent arm and no contemporaneous E2 core-only hold arm. In addition, the supplied stoichiometry note requires recalculation if the acrylic contributes OH or another NCO-reactive group, but the proposal does not specify a functionality audit before treating the modifier as non-reactive. The two registered modifier axes do not move together here, so acrylic-versus-tackifier confounding is avoided; however, acrylic chemistry, dilution, possible stoichiometric change, and preparation-state effects remain entangled.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No direct-observable claim becomes unsupported, but the distinction between a directly measured candidate drift and a model-dependent reference prediction could be obscured.
objections.objection: The primary observable itself survives this attack surface. SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 values in each 120 C trajectory and requires no regression, extrapolation, shared-shape fit, or imputation. The weakness lies in the external E1-based prediction used for interpretation, not in reading the candidate's SI_15_60.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A mixed or borderline pair of repeats could be classified post hoc, weakening the claimed prospective falsification and acceptance rules even though extreme unanimous results remain adjudicable.
objections.objection: The protocol can physically produce SI_15_60 at or above 7.61%, so H-RESIN's stated falsification criterion is attainable. However, 'repeated SI_15_60' is not operationally defined: with at least two independent repeats, the proposal does not state whether both repeats, their mean, or a confidence interval must cross 7.61%, 5.61%, or 3.80%. This matters because the supplied E2 measurements show large between-preparation viscosity-scale variation, including a 3.57x max/min ratio at 120 C, and the proposal already anticipates repeat disagreement.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result could support or reject formulation-level rheological prediction rules, but claims about encounter frequency or specialization of the acrylic axis to viscosity-level relocation would remain unsupported.
objections.objection: No use of withheld follow-up identity or outcome is evident. The scope problem is instead that M-HOLD-120 measures only macroscopic viscosity drift. It cannot establish H-RESIN's stated causal explanation of reduced 'encounter frequency of reaction-capable species,' nor can the hold experiment alone establish H-DUAL's assertion that the acrylic axis principally relocates viscosity level. The proposal's own measurement requirements call for a matched viscosity anchor, but the selected experiment card is only S1C49::M-HOLD-120.

skeptic.recommended_change: Run a pre-specified matched set under identical preparation and 120 C hold conditions: an E2 core-only control, S1C49 with 20% acrylic, a 20% verified non-reactive diluent control at phi_r = 0.80, and an acrylic-plus-minor-tackifier arm at the same acrylic loading. Use at least three independent preparations per arm, audit acrylic OH/NCO-reactive functionality and recalculate true stoichiometry before testing, include the planned matched viscosity-level anchor, and predefine whether classification uses every repeat or a mean with a confidence interval. Use the measured E2 control to estimate the core-specific dilution prediction; pre-register any resulting amendment to the E1-based rule before examining modified-arm outcomes.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The 7.61% H-CORE prediction is extrapolated from the single E1 hold run even though S1C49 uses the compositionally and stoichiometrically different E2 reactive core, for which no hold baseline exists. This prevents a deviation from being uniquely assigned to superlinear acrylic suppression.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.
